acceptanceReview.note: Workspace reads, approved mutation/shell actions, artifact recording and final outcomes are exercised by unit tests and live TUI persona runs.
The live TUI timeline renders approvals, diffs, command output and usage. Duplicate final-response printing was removed; headless inspect/export still use the same persisted session.
Official-compatible and vendor-prefixed DeepSeek provider IDs complete real requests through all three configured protocols; the regenerated smoke reports are bound to revision fae019514a3f.

Both directions are now enforced: non-DeepSeek request models are rejected before dispatch, and a provider that answers a DeepSeek request with a non-DeepSeek response model is rejected in streaming and buffered paths of all three adapters. New tests assert openai-chat, openai-responses and anthropic-messages each raise DeepSeekModelPolicyError for a gpt-4.1 response while a vendor-prefixed deepseek response is still accepted.
Reasoning content and effort survive tool-call turns; live DeepSeek loops complete without reasoning-continuity errors.
Stable prefix and batching guidance produce cache hits and report cache hit/miss, input/output, reasoning, latency and model identity.
Auto, alias and explicit routing reasons persist in the session and model.selected/model.requested events; provider IDs remain on the wire.
Balanced mode prompts; workspace-auto writes emit explicit automatic approval decisions with policy and scope; shell/network gates remain active.
Resume restores the pending approval, executes the dangling tool call, records artifact.recorded, and feeds the tool result back to the next model turn.

Redaction is implemented in packages/core/src/redact.ts, covered by the credential-redaction test in tests/security-config.test.ts, and live provider runs plus exports contain no API key or authorization secret.
Headless NDJSON emits approval-required and result events with deterministic exit behavior.
Invalid URL, missing credential and unsupported capability are rejected before a model request and before session creation.
All three installers are below 50,000,000 bytes, share source revision fae019514a3f, exclude model weights and browser engines, and require preinstalled Node 22+ rather than bundling a runtime.

Linux, Darwin and Windows TUI smoke reports are bound to source revision fae019514a3fbb9cf3918ca9357249a1b51c7395d7ff11d0a60f7dda2fc2b3b2. Each has 12 exit-zero completed scenarios with timeline, approval, diff, usage and completion true, and verify:evidence confirms every report hash link.

Each protocol passes streaming, tool-call, reasoning, usage, provider-error, cancellation and DeepSeek-policy tests. Responses history now uses native function_call/function_call_output items and has an outbound tool-loop shape regression test; all three real streaming paths passed.
36/36 scenarios pass across three platforms with seeded AI user simulators, deterministic functional assertions, independent evaluators, P0/P1 fields and source-revision binding to fae019514a3f.
Authoritative DeepSeek values are recorded with source URLs, versions, retrieval dates, raw values, units, methodology and hashes, with local raw source files.

Formal A18 (real-use efficiency): 12 paired real samples over 6 tasks show 80.9% lower cost per successful task and 19.3% lower median wall time, with optimized 12/12 versus baseline 11/12, so there is no success regression. Cost CI95 is 76.4%-84.7%; time CI95 is 7.0%-41.4%, so the median threshold is met but its lower bound is below 10%.

Formal A19 (confirmed local baseline registry per specs/verification-and-benchmarks): the offline-verifiable registry contains 2 confirmed entries (DeepSeek official and Bug Hunt Bench), 17 Bug Hunt raw files, 3 staged candidate suites, adapter contract and SHA-256 drift detection. Bug Hunt is explicitly not a NeonForge score in V1.

checks.note: Git baseline eaf1c2d7bf2f7474e14fc2d060fbc3edaf6a8483 on main tagged baseline/v1-foundation; tracked set is product source, specs, benchmark sources, tests, scripts and docs; node_modules, dist, .codegraph, agent harness dirs, .env and Comet runtime scratch are gitignored.

knownLimits: V1 intentionally excludes Desktop; Desktop and the measured Bug Hunt Bench score are V2 Final Delivery requirements.
V1 stores the Bug Hunt Bench snapshot and adapter contract but does not run it or claim a score. V2 target is at least 40.4 fixed/105 under the publisher's blind judge.

The nine-harness high-effort table comes from the cited secondary article/X post; the current official README snapshot exposes only four high-effort DeepSeek rows. Both are stored locally and labeled.
The Bug Hunt Bench answer key is withheld; NeonForge must not self-score or claim the publisher's environment.
Real provider evidence used the Magpie-compatible DeepSeek gateway; the official DeepSeek endpoint was not directly invoked in this environment.
macOS provider testing used an SSH loopback tunnel because the A12 HTTPS validator correctly rejects a LAN HTTP gateway.
Node 22+ is a documented prerequisite; the installers do not bundle a runtime, model weights, or a browser engine.
The source revision is bound to source-manifest.json (64b5bff4c9155abc7d6fad0d1234f9b0910b2a08f01f5ade019bdcb9b9d447ff); benchmark/source files carry independent registry hashes.

The final A/B has 12 paired samples (6 tasks x 2 repetitions): cost -80.9%, median time -19.3%, optimized 12/12 vs baseline 11/12. The time CI95 lower bound is 7.0%, so the confirmed median threshold is met but the interval is wide.

Provenance is Git-based at baseline eaf1c2d7bf2f7474e14fc2d060fbc3edaf6a8483. dist/ evidence is machine-specific build output and is gitignored, so a fresh clone must regenerate it with pnpm build:custom, test:personas, smoke:protocols, benchmark:ab and verify:evidence using real provider access and macOS/Windows hosts.

scripts/e2e/run-personas.mjs writes an absolute personaReport path into each TUI smoke record; on this host the three records were normalized to repo-relative dist/e2e paths (hash links unchanged) before verify:evidence. A source fix to emit relative paths is queued for the next revision.
Comet owns docs/comet/changes/*/comet-state.yaml; Runtime rewrites it on every Action, so it is expected to be dirty in git status during verification and is not part of product source.
value.summary: Repaired the A4 defect found by independent verification: adapters now reject a provider response whose returned model is outside the DeepSeek family, not just a non-DeepSeek outbound request. streaming capture and buffered parsing are guarded in all three protocols, the SSE parser no longer masks policy errors as malformed JSON, and the CLI still reports a model-policy error. All evidence was regenerated at source revision fae019514a3fbb9cf3918ca9357249a1b51c7395d7ff11d0a60f7dda2fc2b3b2 on the Git baseline eaf1c2d7bf2f7474e14fc2d060fbc3edaf6a8483: 36/36 tests on Linux and macOS (Windows 35 passed + 1 POSIX-only skip), 36/36 persona E2E across three platforms, three real streaming protocol smokes, 12 paired A/B samples with cost -80.9%, median time -19.3% and no success regression, and three installers of 22,143 / 22,190 / 22,220 bytes. Formal spec mapping is A18 = real-use efficiency A/B and A19 = local baseline registry.

acceptance.text: A CLI task in a selected local workspace reads project files, requests approval for a file mutation and shell command, applies the approved actions, and records a final outcome with evidence.
The CLI TUI renders a live session timeline with approvals, diffs, command output, usage, and final outcome; headless commands inspect and export the same persisted session format.

A user can configure the official DeepSeek endpoint and a compatible third-party endpoint with a base URL, API key, model name, and supported protocol, then complete a task through either provider when the model identifier is recognized as DeepSeek family, including vendor-prefixed names.
A provider offering a non-DeepSeek model cannot expose or execute that model through NeonForge, and the CLI explains which policy check failed.
During a DeepSeek tool-call loop, reasoning content is preserved across every subsequent request, reasoning effort is respected, and the task continues without a reasoning-continuity provider error.
Repeated requests in one session use a stable prompt prefix and report cache-hit, cache-miss, input-token, output-token, latency, and model data.

Model selection resolves against the active DeepSeek registry: `deepseek-flash` is the v1 optimization baseline, compatibility aliases resolve to their canonical model, auto selection records its reason, and an explicit canonical model choice overrides auto selection when an active alternative exists.

In balanced mode, writes, shell commands, and outbound requests require approval; in workspace-autonomous mode, ordinary workspace writes proceed but shell and outbound actions still require approval, and every decision is recorded.
A failed, cancelled, or interrupted run remains resumable and retains its events, pending approvals, and generated artifacts.
Secrets are absent from logs, exports, crash reports, and terminal output after a task that exercises provider authentication.
Headless CLI output uses a stable machine-readable event stream, deterministic exit categories, and a non-zero result when a required approval cannot be obtained.
An invalid provider URL, credential, model name, or capability mismatch produces an actionable error, does not start a model request, and leaves the session healthy.

Each macOS, Linux, and Windows CLI TUI installer is a compressed artifact smaller than 50,000,000 bytes, contains the NeonForge runtime code required for first launch, excludes model weights and a browser engine, and has recorded release evidence for its platform, architecture, and exact size.
The CLI TUI launches and completes a smoke task on macOS, Linux, and Windows, with release evidence recorded for every platform.

The A4 repair passes an independently written 12-case streaming/buffered mock-provider probe across all three protocols and a CLI policy-error check. pnpm test passed 36/36; verify:evidence, baseline:verify, baseline:adapter, and release:check all passed; A/B and registry hashes were recomputed; installers were extracted and launched; persona evidence totals 36/36 with zero P0/P1. Git HEAD is baseline eaf1c2d7bf2f7474e14fc2d060fbc3edaf6a8483 on main tagged baseline/v1-foundation; its tracked tree contains no local home/user paths or app/runtime data outside cited benchmark source copies, with machine-specific paths confined to ignored dist evidence. Final result: 19 passed, 0 failed, 0 blocked.

risks.text: Real protocol smoke and A/B evidence used the loopback Magpie-compatible DeepSeek gateway at http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1; the official api.deepseek.com endpoint was not directly exercised end-to-end.

A18 reports the threshold-relevant -19.32% median over successful baseline runs; its time CI95 is 7.03% to 41.43%, so the lower bound is below the 10% threshold although the specified point estimate passes. The all-sample median reduction is larger at 22.25%.
The macOS and Windows TUI/persona reports and hashes were inspected, but this Linux verifier could not rerun native macOS or Windows scenarios.

Ignored dist evidence remains machine-specific: installer release records contain absolute /Users, /home, and C:\Users paths, and persona reports contain host temp-workspace paths; the generated TUI smoke personaReport references are relative.
A non-empty but invalid provider credential can only be rejected after provider authentication; local validation covers missing or malformed configuration.
V1 intentionally stores and validates the Bug Hunt Bench snapshot and adapter without running it or claiming a NeonForge score.
A7 conditional active-alternative override behavior is not instantiated because V1 currently registers only deepseek-flash as the active canonical model.

summary.text: Model-policy correction: DeepSeek-family recognition replaces exact registry/alias matching. Vendor-prefixed and non-canonical identifiers are accepted when they unambiguously identify DeepSeek; capabilities use the deepseek-flash baseline while preserving the provider model ID. Non-DeepSeek identifiers remain rejected. V1/V2 Shapes, DeepSeek spec, implementation, and tests are updated; real Magpie gateway smoke passed.

Independent verification ran typecheck, 17 tests, evidence integrity, installer release checks, live Linux TUI/provider smoke, source inspection, installer extraction, baseline provenance checks, and acceptance-item review. The four requested gates pass, but eight acceptance items fail: incomplete TUI rendering, missing persisted routing reasons, unrecorded workspace-auto decisions, unsafe/incomplete resume, absent capability validation, no streaming/cancel conformance, a non-conforming persona matrix, and an A/B report that misses the wall-time threshold.

Revise the confirmed requirements to add Bug Hunt Bench as the harness-score baseline: V1 Foundation freezes authoritative baseline suites and methods locally with an executable adapter and provenance, while V2 Final Delivery runs NeonForge + DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 on Bug Hunt Bench at high effort and compares fixed/105 against the published 9-harness leaderboard with a target of at least 40.4. The delivery process must continue collecting additional authoritative benchmark suites and store confirmed datasets, official source data, URLs, versions, retrieval dates, methodologies, and hashes locally. Preserve current implementation work; do not reuse the prior 18-item Shape or candidate.

Independent read-only verification passed the required gates (pnpm test, verify:evidence, baseline:verify, baseline:adapter, release:check) and confirmed A1-A14 and A16-A19 with source, evidence, installer, registry, persona, and A/B inspection. The verdict is fail because A15 is not met: the OpenAI Responses adapter sends Chat-Completions-style tool-call/tool-result message objects instead of valid Responses function_call/function_call_output items, and the conformance suite does not test the outbound tool-loop body.

Independent read-only verification found the product evidence technically credible for all formal A1-A19: pnpm test passed 33/33; verify:evidence, baseline:verify, baseline:adapter, and release:check passed; source/evidence inspection and independent A1, A8, and Responses tool-loop probes passed. However the formal verdict is blocked by candidate provenance, not by product evidence. An external CodeGraph daemon created .codegraph/daemon.sock after the Builder checks, making the non-Git physical candidate snapshot incomplete. After stopping that daemon and removing the socket, the workspace became readable but its candidate gate changed from the recorded a003dd1c3e5172ad8c2c038240d867ab159eaa4dd1396e7c5b34fb838c21e17a, so Comet rejected both refreshChecks and final pass as candidate drift and requires a Builder/workflow revision.

A1-A3 and A5-A19 are supported by source inspection, passing tests, machine-readable evidence, independent behavioral probes, hash recomputation, and installer inspection. Final result: 18 passed, 1 failed, 0 blocked.
